content.title: About
content.content: Cheese quesadilla is a classic Mexican dish consisting of a thin corn or flour tortilla filled with melted cheese. When cooked, the cheese becomes stretchy and aromatic, while the tortilla turns crisp.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “quesadilla” derives from the Spanish “quesada,” meaning “cheese pie.”
Common cheeses used are cheddar, Monterey Jack, or Mexican “Oaxaca” cheese.
It can be served as a snack or a main course, often accompanied by salsa, guacamole, or sour cream.
Tortillas can be made from corn or wheat flour, each giving a distinct flavor and texture.

items.title: Calcium source
items.content: Cheese provides a good amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: The cheese supplies complete animal protein that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 in cheese supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Probiotics (when using fermented cheeses)
items.content: Certain cheeses contain live cultures that may benefit gut health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Combining tortilla carbs with cheese fats provides quick, sustained energy.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience digestive discomfort after eating cheese quesadillas.

items.title: Milk‑protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein can trigger severe reactions, including anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many cheeses are salty; excess sodium can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Quesadillas are relatively high in calories, so portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Trans fats (in some processed cheeses)
items.content: Certain commercial cheese products may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut the quesadilla into wedges and serve hot with dips such as salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. It can be eaten by hand or sliced into smaller pieces for children.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked quesadillas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in a skillet or oven to restore crispness. Frozen quesadillas keep for up to 2 months when wrapped tightly in plastic.
